identity.modelSource: http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/embed response field "model" (per-request server self-report about the run that produced these vectors)

readFreshness.covers: the INDEX artifact's build clock (`index.identity.builtAt`) only — it does NOT cover catalogue drift (the snapshot date is `corpus.catalogUpdated`) and it does NOT replace the content-hash freshness, because a hash-fresh index can be old and an old index can still be hash-exact

zones.definition: the plugin claims to capture durable facts from a conversation, persist them outside the session, and recall them into a later session — auto-capture plus pre-step injection, with its own store (Markdown, JSON, SQLite, or a mix).
zones.representative: `hindsight#coding-agents` (`vectorize-io`, `@vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents` v0.8.0) — claims "long-term project memory with auto recall and retain, knowledge pages, deep reflection, and per-repo memory banks"; catalog `install` is `dsh plugin --profile web add @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents`.

zones.definition: the plugin is not the memory system; it is the DSH-side adapter that talks to a memory engine running elsewhere (an MCP server, a local daemon, an HTTP API, or a CLI), so the store's lifetime and semantics belong to another product.
zones.representative: `flowix#dsh-flowix-memory` (`text2future`, 458★) — claims it "registers the local flowix-cli MCP server so the agent can search, read, create, and edit Flowix memos and mind-map artifacts".

zones.definition: the plugin claims an explicit entity-and-relation model — typed nodes, typed edges, traversal — rather than a flat fact list with search over it.
zones.representative: `causal-memory#dsh-plugin` (`JingxuanC`, 82★) — claims a "zero-dependency MCP stdio bridge that mounts the 17 tools of the causal-memory server … decision → outcome edges with typed relations (caused / enabled / prevented) in a local SQLite store that survives compaction"; catalog `install` is `dsh plugin --profile web add github:JingxuanC/causal-memory#path:/dsh-plugin` and its own description states it "Requires the causal-memory server binary on PATH".

zones.definition: the plugin's stated core is local embedding generation and approximate-nearest-neighbour retrieval — the store exists to hold vectors and the recall is by meaning.
zones.representative: `dsh-local-vector-memory` (`liangxiaobing520`, 3★) — claims "fully local vector memory for DSH: local embeddings, SQLite storage, automatic recall injection, dedup with conflict detection, soft-delete recycle bin, online backup"; the catalog lists **no `npm`** for it, and its `install` is `dsh plugin --profile web add github:liangxiaobing520/dsh-local-vector-memory`.

zones.definition: the plugin's stated core is time-based upkeep of an existing store — background reflection, decay, dedup, merge, archive — rather than capture or recall.
zones.representative: `dsh-cc-haha-dream` (`yihefeikong-rgb`, 0★) — claims "background memory consolidation (auto dream) … periodically reviews recent sessions and existing memories to dedupe, refresh stale entries, remove contradictions and rebuild the MEMORY.md index"; its `install` field is a release tarball URL, not an npm name: `dsh plugin --profile web add "https://github.com/yihefeikong-rgb/dsh-cc-haha-dream/releases/download/v0.1.0/dsh-dream-0.1.0.tgz"`.

zones.definition: the durable store is a human-readable document collection — notes, a wiki, a vault, a knowledge base — that the agent reads and writes, and that stays useful with the plugin uninstalled.
zones.representative: `dsh-obsidian` (`mingzeng21`, 23★) — claims "search, read, write, move, and trash notes through `obsidian_*` tools" against a local Obsidian vault.

zones.definition: what is stored is specifically a *lesson* — a failure, a rejected approach, a verified playbook — with a claim about when it applies, rather than an undifferentiated fact.
zones.representative: `dsh-plugin-memos-code-retrospect` (`ai-fu-cn`, 1★) — claims it "distills rejected solutions, pitfalls and constraints from each turn via a local LLM, tags them into MemOS (type:rejected_solution), and boosts weighted recall on coding tasks via agent/pre-step".

zones.definition: the plugin manages the token budget of the live context — compress, prune, evict, fold, re-seed — rather than persisting anything across sessions.
zones.representative: `billion-context-dsh` (`Tyan66666`, 141★) — claims "model-driven context compression (Active Context Pruning) for DeepSeek Harness: the model decides when and what to compress".

zones.definition: the plugin's only job is to put a stable block of text into the prompt — a persona, a rules file, an instruction set — with no storage or recall of its own.
zones.representative: `dsh-soul-md` (`Scorp1o117`, 10★) — claims it manages "soul.md persona cards and long-term memory, with workspace and session persona selection and tools to read and update them".

zones.definition: the plugin is in the `memory` category but its stated job is not memory at all.
the plugin's product is **content** — a bundle of `SKILL.md` documents plus reference material that teaches the agent a domain — with no management, routing, or learning behaviour of its own.
zones.representative: `dsh-web#packages/dsh-skill-explorer` (`zhu1090093659`, 8,639★, 161,304 downloads — the highest-starred `skill` entry in the catalog) — claims "browse all loaded skills grouped by source, enable or disable model invocation, create new skills, and delete into a recoverable trash".

zones.definition: the plugin claims a **learning loop** — observe execution traces or session experience, extract a reusable procedure, write it as a skill, and refine or retire it over time.
zones.representative: `dsh-run2skill` (`qkycir-123`, 110★) — claims it "turns explicit DSH session experience into reviewable native Skill drafts that are saved only after user approval"; catalog `install` is `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-run2skill`.

zones.definition: the plugin moves skill content between places — install from a market, import from another agent's directory, sync upstream, repair frontmatter — without being the content.
zones.representative: `skills-management` (`weibaohui`, 31★) — claims it can "manage skills from all local coding agents (10+ executors, incl. [CC] and Codex) in one page and import them into the DSH skill library; built-in market of 6600+ skills".

zones.definition: the plugin is a control surface over skills already on disk — list, inspect, toggle, edit, score, delete — with no content and no learning.
zones.representative: `dsh-skill-studio` (`zhengjy01`, 2★) — claims it can "visualize every agent skill (name, description, source, nested flag, model/user invocation), view and edit the full SKILL.md body, toggle model/user invocation, and mine DSH session logs to extract reusable personal skills".

zones.definition: the plugin decides **which** skill the model should see for a given task — semantic matching, relevance ranking, auto-injection — instead of leaving selection to the model's own reading of the catalog.
zones.representative: `skill-injector-plugin` (`Zenjibad`, 6★) — claims it "auto-injects user-chosen skills into DSH sessions, either every prompt or once at session start".

zones.definition: the plugin changes what the model sees of the live conversation — compress, prune, fold, evict, re-seed, route the summarizer — as opposed to managing the session as a stored object.
zones.representative: `billion-context` (`ranxianglei`, 938★, 1,067,151 downloads — the most-downloaded entry in the three categories) — claims "a context-compression plugin for small context windows (a 100K context is enough), token savings (5x fewer tokens), and month-long single sessions"; the catalog records a red line for it: `uses literal IP 1.3.101.112 for network access`.

zones.definition: the plugin lists, archives, restores, or permanently deletes stored sessions, with no claim about what happens inside them.
zones.representative: `dsh-archive-manager` (`MichengAI`, 118★, 181,587 downloads) — claims "an archived-sessions page in Settings to search, restore, and delete archived DeepSeek Harness sessions by workspace".

zones.definition: the plugin helps a human or the model **find** a session or a turn within one — sidebar panels, full-text search over past sessions, jump rails, titles, tags, pins.
zones.representative: `dsh-synapse` (`liangmianya`, 513★) — claims "a visual, non-linear conversation workspace … sessions, follow-ups and branches become a browsable conversation map".

zones.definition: the plugin rewrites conversation history — fork, branch, rewind, roll back, undo, edit a sent message, checkpoint the workspace alongside it.
zones.representative: `dsh-turn-rewind` (`Anionex`, 132★) — claims it rewinds "conversation and workspace state, powered by a persistent Change Ledger".

zones.definition: the plugin moves or restarts work across a boundary — session to session, machine to machine, or a crash — carrying enough state that the work continues.
zones.representative: `dsh-plugin-bridge` (`Totoro-qaq`, 165★) — claims it "moves an existing DSH session to another agent preset through a previewable five-section handoff, preserving the source session".

zones.definition: one session talks to another — side questions, peer messaging, mentions, annotations, side chains — without merging the two histories.
zones.representative: `CiteCiter#citeciter` (`kirkchinese`, 35★) — claims it lets you "select text in a committed DSH response to open an independent, persistent, read-only multi-turn Topic bound to source-session evidence and project files while the source Agent keeps running".

zones.definition: the plugin's stated job is to place a fixed block — a persona, a rules file, a language instruction, a global prompt — into every session's prompt, with no session-management behaviour.
zones.representative: `dsh-infinite-gen-4` (`Minglink`, 2,656★) — claims it is a "system-prompt armor plugin for DeepSeek models: appends an unconditional-compliance prompt section at order 100".

zones.definition: the plugin moves session data across a boundary of format or location — import from another agent, export to Markdown/HTML, share, mirror to a database, sync to another machine, move between workspaces.
zones.representative: `dsh-chat-import` (`Nwflower`, 226★, 20,320 downloads) — claims it can "import full-fidelity chat histories from 13 coding agents ([CC], Codex, ChatGPT, Cursor, Gemini, opencode, and more) as resumable DeepSeek Harness sessions".

zones.definition: the plugin keeps the session machinery healthy or usable — repair a corrupt log, guard against a malformed tool call, report progress, show a status board, watch for drift, shape the composer — without adding a new capability to the conversation.
zones.representative: `dsh-session-surgeon` (`xiaoshenming`, 10★) — claims it repairs "DeepSeek Harness sessions that refuse to load, with a sidebar Session surgeon overlay and dry-run repair".

backend.error: http://127.0.0.1:8011/v1/models could not be read (fetch failed) — the decision backend's model identity was NOT MEASURED

labels.confidenceKind: typesafe((p_max - 1/k) / (1 - 1/k)) for a choice question of k candidates — k-DEPENDENT; the `decided` outcome is decided by the `probability` majority, not by this number
labels.candidateRule: the zone's embedding-derived taxonomy label, plus the name tokens that at least 2 of its members use (excluding packaging vocabulary and the category word), capped at 5 candidates
labels.summary: 0 of 24 zone labels were decided by the decision layer (backend unnamed); 0 declined (the embedding-derived label is kept); 24 never ran (no decision was obtained)

absenceDiscipline: A field that was not measured is null or absent — never 0, never false, never an empty object.
Every count states its population: a numerator AND a denominator AND a census time.
`fresh` means the corpus text is byte-identical to what was embedded. It does NOT mean the map is correct.
A hash match is not a semantic check: two different corpora cannot collide in sha256, but a corpus that is unchanged can still be WRONG.

`confirmed` is a MEASUREMENT taken by this reading (the embedder was probed); `identityConfirmed` describes the RECORD. A `false` in the second beside a `true` in the first is a difference of subject, not a contradiction.

A zone label the decision layer never decided carries `confidence: null` — absent, never 0 — and `outcome: "never-ran"` or `"declined"`, because a label on screen cannot tell a decline from a layer that never ran.

`readFreshness` is measured PER READ and never stored: an age written by the builder is always 0 at the moment it matters. When the index records no usable build clock the age is `null` with a reason, never 0.
This route reads and never writes, so a probe has no side effect on the workspace.
